uniequip_002_botany:
I hear someone calling my name. The sound comes from very far away, and it leaves me unable to fall asleep again.
Every night the call arrives right on schedule; some nights I brew a cup of coffee and sit at my desk waiting for it. I do not know whether it is a hallucination. I would rather believe it is the result of some kind of signal interference. The Medical Department prescribed me something to settle the nerves and help me sleep, but in truth I have no need of it.
There it is again.
The voice is deeply familiar. I counted, one by one, through everyone I have ever met in my memory, and none of them matched. Mother's voice was far gentler; the playmate from next door died of pneumonia at six. As for my sister, she never called me that way—
My sister would only gaze into my eyes for a long time, as though trying to make out the structure of my soul, and then turn and walk away... No—what was it I just remembered?
Cold, dry air, the sort that makes you want to sneeze. That was in... Bresk? I cannot forget that warm passageway. I looked at the Grand Duchess's back, waiting for her to step out of the shadows so that I might clasp those hands once more. I waited a long while, but she did not move at all. Perhaps all she needed was for the citizens to see with their own eyes that I had walked into that 'palace,' and nothing more. Was it then that someone out on the street was calling to me?
No. It was not then.
Perhaps it was in Deity Grypherburg, when I walked into the Imperial Polytechnic University with my letter of admission in hand. I was not the only commoner stuffed into that Garden of Nobility for the sake of somebody's record in office, but I was the only Elafia there at the time. I stood in the courtyard and looked at the michelia that had been transplanted from Yan at enormous cost. The nobles donated five heaters for the sake of one tree, and still it did not survive a single flowering season. Was it then? I picked a white petal up off the ground, and someone called down to me from an upper floor—only to sneer at that horn of mine remade into an antenna...
No. I look at the empty coffee cup, and my thoughts come to a halt. In the bottom of the white porcelain, a face seems to be reflected.
I feel wind and snow scraping past my cheek, as though I have returned to the day I parted from my sister. I had fallen in the snow, holding the little radio she once gave me, tuned to the channel the two of us had agreed on, my mouth open wide and no idea what to say—
To call her back? To apologize? To accuse her? No, none of it was right. On all this earth there was not one sentence that belonged to me in that moment. All I had was my name.
'Tishina Viktorovna Belyaeva!'
I heard my own voice. After nearly twenty years, I heard once more the voice I cried out with then.
I think of my unfinished paper. Perhaps not one of the signals we send out has ever truly vanished. Every time a signal strikes the Originium particles in the air, in the earth, in lake water, it stirs an echo. Signals born of Originium Arts grow fainter and fainter, but they never disappear entirely!
They go on echoing through your life—ten years, twenty years, a hundred years—and one day you catch hold of them again. I heard myself calling out at five years old; I heard the words of thanks I read aloud for the Grand Duchess; I heard myself reciting in the attic where I hid at the end of term. And I heard, from the Katorga District, all those...
I saw those formless signals circling me like stars. They are greetings I sent, without meaning to, from my past to my future. Not once have I ever been far from any of the days I have lived.
